plan: Since the sealed bid acts as an automatic exit point in an ascending clock auction with 2 other bidders, this effectively mimics a second-price auction structure. In such mechanisms, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy — it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I pay only the second-highest bid (not my own), maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $42.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the ascending clock mechanism means I pay the second-highest bid if I win, determined by my sealed bid acting as my exit point), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable trades.

This is effectively a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay, and I'll win only if others' bids are lower, paying the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value ($48) is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds price) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win.
